prompt: Some people think that schools should teach students according to their academic abilities, while others believe that it is better to have students with different abilities to study together. Discuss both views and give your own opinion.
essay:
Many people argue that ability-based teaching should be used in schools, whereas others claim that mixed-ability classes are more beneficial in many ways. This essay will discuss both perspectives before explaining why I believe mixed-ability education is the better approach.

On the one hand, teaching students according to their academic level can make lessons more efficient and productive. In a class of high achievers, extra explanations may not be necessary, allowing teachers to cover more complex topics in less time. Furthermore, this teaching system helps teachers identify highly capable students and support them further. In many cases, teachers are more focused on weaker students, causing high achievers to receive less attention. Ability-based teaching can prevent this issue. Similarly, separating weaker students enables them to learn at their own pace. They can ask for clearer explanations without feeling embarrassed or pressured. This can often be seen in schools where struggling students hesitate to ask questions because they fear slowing others down.

On the other hand, labelling some children as stronger and others as weaker at an early stage of their academic life could do more harm than good. Separating children too early may cause them to lose confidence and ambition, preventing those who develop academic skills more slowly from reaching their full potential. By contrast, mixed-ability classes allow students to work together and learn from one another. When a student who understands a topic clearly explains it to a classmate, both students benefit. The student giving the explanation develops a deeper understanding of the topic, while the other is able to learn in a more relaxed and less intimidating environment.

In conclusion, while some people believe that an ability-based approach is more effective, others support mixed-ability education. In my view, the best solution is to maintain mostly mixed-ability classes while still providing additional support for weaker students and extra challenges for high achievers.
